To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selectivity of 65 protein kinase inhibitors has been profiled against 70 80 enzymes.

the small molecule inhibitors of the 65 protein kinases that have been reported as specific inhibitors of individual protein kinases are not as selective in vitro as originally claimed, that there is no single compound that is specific for any protein kinase, that the specificity of many of the inhibitors that we have tested has been overestimated and, as a consequence of these observations, that there is a need for caution in the interpretation of data obtained from studies using small molecule inhibitors.

the small molecule protein kinase inhibitors SB 203580, SB 202190, PI103, wortmannin, PP1, PP2, PD 184352, PD 032590, Akt I, Akt I, rapamycin, CT 99021, BI D1870, SL0101, FMK, D4476, VX680 and roscovitin are specific inhibitors of the p38 MAPK, PI3K, Src family kinases, MKK1
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel protein kinase inhibitors, their use in cell biology and the development of new assays for protein kinase inhibitor discovery.

the identification and characterization of novel small molecule inhibitors of the protein kinases, which are of potential use as therapeutics or as tools to study the physiological roles of protein kinases.
the discovery of new inhibitors of protein kinates and their use in the study of protein kinases in cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physiological roles of most protein kinases are unknown.
the physiological roles of many protein kinases remain to be established, and that the use of specific protein kinase inhibitors to address this question should be undertaken with great caution.
the physiological roles of protein kinases remain unknown, and that the best way of assessing their roles in vivo is to use gene knockout mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of small molecule protein kinase inhibitors to assess the roles of these enzymes is fraught with difficulties.
the specificity of most of the inhibitors we have analysed is too poor for their use to be recommended.

there are few protein kinase inhibitors that are specific enough to be used to study the functions of individual protein kinases in cells, although some are specific enough for particular protein kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to make any useful conclusions from the use of a single compound to inhibit the activity of any protein kinase.

it is essential to profile the selectivity of any new small molecule inhibitor against a panel of protein kinases and to use the inhibitor in combination with other compounds with different selectivities to be able to draw meaningful physiological conclusions from experiments.
the specificity of inhibitors should always be tested in parallel to the biological effects of the inhibitor in cells.
